To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have developed a ternary self-assembling monolayer (aptamers/HDT/MCH) on screen printed electrodes for impedance-based aptasensing.
the optimisation and characterization of aptasensors with ternary SAM layers can lead to the development of robust, anti-fouling, and sensitive biosensors.
the optimisation of the anti-fouling aptasensor is highly dependent on the type of the gold surface used for the electrode preparation, as well as on the ratio of aptamers to HDT in the ternary SAM.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and optimisation of aptasensors with enhanced anti-foulability.
the design of an impedance-based aptasensor for detection of proteins.
the optimisation and development of aptasensors based on self-assembled monomers for detection of proteins in complex samples.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the aptasensor presented here can be used for detection of human thrombin in real biological samples with high sensitivity and specificity and without interference from other proteins.
the aptasensor has a high specificity for thrombin with low non-specific binding, which is a key requirement for aptasensors in real biological samples.

the aptasensor with the highest sensitivity and selectivity was obtained using 1:1:2 ratio between aptameric DNA, 1,6-HDT and 1-meraptohexanol, respectively, and incubation of the electrodes in 50 mM PBS buffer, pH 7.0, at room temperature.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the optimisation of ternary SAM layers is essential for the development of anti-fouling aptasensors with high sensitivity, specificity and selectivity.
a highly specific, anti-fouling and stable aptasensor has been developed and characterised for human thrombin detection.
the ternary self-assembly monolayer (aptamers, HDT and MCH) is a highly promising platform for aptasensor construction, which can be used for detection of proteins in biological samples.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ternary self-assembly monolayer is an effective approach to generate a robust and anti-fouled sensing layer for impedance based aptasensor development.
the ternary SAM layer is a promising approach for development of anti-fouling aptasensors.
the anti-fouling resistance can be enhanced using ternary SAM layers and this can lead to the development of highly sensitive aptasensors with low background noise.
